subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity — GPU mix, TPS snapshot & next decision call
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity — GPU mix, TPS snapshot & next decision call

Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets SLA and cost goals. Short summary of what I heard from your infra and product teams: 

- Target production SLOs: p95 token-latency ~700ms for typical 512-token responses; p99 < 1.5s for burst windows.
- Traffic shape: primary US region, two daily peaks (coinciding with east coast business hours), estimated peak sustained TPS = 120 requests/sec (inbound requests), average request = 420 input tokens + 200 generation tokens (avg total ~620 tokens).
- Traffic variability: 80% of calls are short (prompt-heavy, <200 gen tokens), 20% are long generation jobs (~1000+ tokens) for batch workflows.
- Security: VPC peering required; logs to customer-managed S3.
- Compliance: SOC-2 evidence request in procurement (we'll share SOC-2 PDF).

Next steps we committed to on the call:
1) You’ll share the raw load spreadsheet (I noticed infra already uploaded a first-pass — thanks).
2) We’ll propose a GPU mix and expected concurrency profile for Dedicated (options for A100 vs H100 vs an L4/H4-style lower-cost candidate).
3) Decide whether Dedicated pool + VPC (private control plane) is needed right away or we start hosted with a predictable Dedicated ramp.
4) Schedule a 30-min sizing call next Wed (Apr 1) to lock SKU and contract term.

I attached a simple worksheet and a one-page SKU summary to start; Ben and Karthik are looped in to propose the initial three configuration options below before the call. If any of the points above are off, correct me in a quick reply.

Thanks — Tessa

--

Thanks Tessa — that matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from infra: 

- Peak TPS is 120 sustained for the east-coast period, but we expect 20% headroom needed for burst to 160 TPS for ~10 minutes several times per day.
- Most critical is keeping p95 latency stable for our conversational flows (~95% of traffic). The long batch jobs can tolerate higher latency if we place them on a lower-priority queue.
- We definitely want VPC (private control plane) from day 1 due to routing and logs requirements.

I’ve asked infra to drop a raw CSV into the Drive link you provided (they just uploaded). Can you include a quick config that shows: (A) sustainable Dedicated pool for 120 TPS with 20% burst; (B) smaller pool + hosted fallback; and (C) cost-optimized option for primarily batch with lower SLA?

—Alex

Subject: RE: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity — GPU mix, TPS snapshot & next decision call

Tessa — drafted the three options Alex asked for. Paste of the short rationale below; I also uploaded a pre-filled tab in clearsight_load_profile_v1.xlsx with throughput assumptions. We should surface expected token-per-second throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) and concurrent request headroom so procurement can compare unit economics.

Option A — Production-dense (aim: keep p95 < 700ms for 512 tokens):
- GPU: H100 (80GB) x24
- Expected steady-state: ~120 TPS (mixed request sizes), with ~20% burst headroom to 150-160 TPS using autoscaling slots.
- Concurrency model: continuous batching with 6-8 request-concurrency per GPU for efficient throughput; KV cache for short conversations to reduce effective token compute by ~18-22%.
- Notes: best latency; highest cost.

Option B — Hybrid fallback (Balanced):
- GPU: A100 (40GB) x28 + Hosted fallback route for overflow
- Expected steady-state: can handle sustained 120 TPS with slightly higher batching (10-12 concurrency per GPU) and fallback to hosted for short spikes beyond 140 TPS.
- Concurrency model: optimize for cost while keeping p95 within 1.0s for common requests.
- Notes: good tradeoff for predictable spend + reduced committed cost.

Option C — Cost-optimized (Batch-first):
- GPU: L4/H4-style (accelerator) x40 or mixed small GPUs; queue long jobs on low-priority pool
- Expected steady-state: handles base load for non-latency-critical batch (~80 TPS equivalent), long jobs scheduled.
- Concurrency model: high batching, larger token-per-second amortization; conversational p95 will be higher.
- Notes: lowest cost; still viable if ClearSight is ok with higher p95 for some flows.

Deliverables for Wed call: a slide with per-option monthly cost estimate, latency P95 projection for 512-token generation, recommended contract term (12 vs 24 mo) and initial rollout plan (canary % using dedicated while keeping hosted as safety). I can draft cost numbers before the call if you want.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — appreciate the quick confirmation from infra. I pulled Ben's options into a one-pager and added an initial cost cadence and recommended next-week milestones. High-level ask for the Apr 1 call (30m):

1) Confirm target SLOs per traffic class (conversational vs batch).
2) Pick preferred SKU approach (A/B/C) and acceptable p95 range for the conversational flow.
3) Confirm VPC + KMS requirements (we will prepare the Private control-plane order form if you want VPC from day 1).

If you’re good with Wed at 10:30am PT I’ll send a calendar invite and Ben will bring the cost slide. If you want a slightly longer slot (45m) to walk procurement, say the word.

Quick note about sizing assumptions we used (so procurement sees the math):
- Avg tokens/call: 620 tokens (420 prompt + 200 gen).
- Effective tokens/sec per H100 (mixed): ~16k tokens/sec under continuous batching for our tuned model; per-A100 ~9-11k tokens/sec depending on quantization; smaller accelerators vary.
- We assume 18% KV cache savings for conversational flows.

I’ll attach the one-pager to the invite. Let me know the time and I’ll lock it in.

Thanks — Tessa
